The molecular mass of a compound with an empirical formula of SO₂ is 256 g/mol. What is the molecular formula?
questions.given: You will not be able to type subscripts. Just type the numbers where they go. For example, S₂O₃ would be typed in as S2O3.
questions.note: SO₂ = 64 g/mol. 256 ÷ 64 = 4, so multiply every subscript by 4.

questions.q: What is the percent by mass of hydrogen in C₂H₈O?
questions.given: Use molar masses with at least 2 decimal places and report your answer to two decimal places. Format answers with a percent sign, like 15.01 % or 15.01%.

What is the percent composition (also called percent mass) of Rh in this formula: Rh₂Cl₂H₄?
questions.given: Molar masses: Rh = 102.91 g/mol  ·  Cl = 35.45 g/mol  ·  H = 1.01 g/mol  ·  round your answer to the 'ones' position (ex: 12.01 = 12).

questions.q: What is the percent composition (also called percent mass) of Cl in this formula: Rh₄Cl₃H₃?
questions.given: Molar masses: Rh = 102.91 g/mol  ·  Cl = 35.45 g/mol  ·  H = 1.01 g/mol  ·  round your answer to the 'ones' position (ex: 12.01 = 12).

questions.q: What is the empirical formula of a compound that contains only cobalt and oxygen if an 8.29 gram sample contains 5.89 grams of cobalt?
questions.note: O = 8.29 − 5.89 = 2.40 g. 5.89 g Co × (1 mol Co / 58.93 g Co) = 0.100 mol; 2.40 g O × (1 mol O / 16.00 g O) = 0.150 mol. Divide by the smallest: 1 : 1.5 → × 2 → Co₂O₃.

questions.q: A 6.341 g sample of a compound is found to have 1.433 grams of nitrogen and no other element except oxygen. What is the empirical formula of the compound?
A hydrocarbon is found to contain 82.66% carbon and no other element except hydrogen. What is the empirical formula?
questions.note: Assume 100 g: 82.66 g C × (1 mol C / 12.01 g C) = 6.883 mol; 17.34 g H × (1 mol H / 1.01 g H) = 17.17 mol. Divide by the smallest: 1 : 2.5 → × 2 → C₂H₅.

questions.q: A compound was discovered whose composition by mass is 85.6% C and 14.4% H. What is the empirical formula for this compound?
questions.given: You will not be able to type subscripts. Just type the numbers where they go. For example, S₂O₃ would be typed in as S2O3.
questions.note: Assume 100 g: 85.6 g C × (1 mol C / 12.01 g C) = 7.13 mol; 14.4 g H × (1 mol H / 1.01 g H) = 14.26 mol. Divide by 7.13: 1 : 2 → CH₂.
